title: Largest open with unramified diagonal in an algebraic stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$. There exists an open substack $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal X$ whose relative diagonal $\mathcal U\to\mathcal U\times_S\mathcal U$ is unramified, and every open substack of $\mathcal X$ with unramified relative diagonal is contained in $\mathcal U$. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids on schemes with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, representability and scheme atlases use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and smooth means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Open substacks are full substacks whose pullback by every scheme is an open subscheme. A representable morphism is unramified if every scheme base change, on etale scheme charts of its algebraic-space source, is unramified in [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus), DM part, with definition-absolute-separated and Tag 050N (lemma-separated-implies-morphism-separated), part (1) for the relative-base convention.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-open-substack-unions], choose a set of representatives of all open substacks of $\mathcal X$. Let $I$ be the subset consisting of those representatives $\mathcal U_i$ whose relative diagonal over $S$ is unramified. Form the algebraic open substack $\mathcal U=\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal U_i$. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal U$, the open subschemes $T_i=T\times_{\mathcal U}\mathcal U_i$ cover $T$. This is a set-indexed union; no quasi-compactness of $\mathcal X$ or finiteness of $I$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks) and 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks), applied to the family in Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus).

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, apply [lem-sfb-unramified-diagonal-etale-atlas] to the algebraic stack $\mathcal U_i$ over $S$. Choose a scheme $W_i$ and a representable surjective etale map $a_i:W_i\to\mathcal U_i$. Its hypothesis is exactly the defining condition for $i\in I$; the criterion is already stated for the relative diagonal over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus), application of Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM); relative-base convention is included in the cited node.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to form the scheme $W=\coprod_{i\in I}W_i$, with its disjoint open summands covering $W$. The objects over $W_i$ given by the composites $W_i\to\mathcal U_i\to\mathcal U$ glue to an object over $W$: on intersections of distinct summands there is only the empty descent datum, and on each summand the overlap isomorphism is the identity. The stack descent axiom in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] therefore gives a map $a:W\to\mathcal U$ restricting to those composites. This map is representable by algebraic spaces: for a scheme $T\to\mathcal U$, $W\times_{\mathcal U}T$ is the base change of the representable diagonal of $\mathcal U$ by $W\times_ST\to\mathcal U\times_S\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus), the disjoint-union atlas construction, with scheme coproduct and stack descent written out.

proof.text: We check etaleness of $a$ on scheme charts, as required by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Fix a scheme $T\to\mathcal U$ and write $E=W\times_{\mathcal U}T$. For an etale scheme chart $P\to E$, inverse images of the summands $W_i\subseteq W$ give an open cover $P=\bigcup_iP_i$. Because $\mathcal U_i\subseteq\mathcal U$ is full, the $i$th open subspace of $E$ is canonically $W_i\times_{\mathcal U_i}T_i$, where $T_i=T\times_{\mathcal U}\mathcal U_i$ is an open subscheme of $T$. Thus $P_i$ is an etale scheme chart of that base change of $a_i$, and $P_i\to T_i$ is etale by the representable etaleness of $a_i$. By clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], $P_i\to T_i\hookrightarrow T$ is etale. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] to the open cover $(P_i)$ to conclude that $P\to T$ is etale. This proves that $a$ is etale. The identifications here are identities of triples in the 2-fibre product, not an assertion that the diagonal's target is covered by the products $\mathcal U_i\times_S\mathcal U_i$.

source.place: Tags 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize), in the atlas construction of Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus).

proof.text: The map $a$ is surjective in the same scheme tests. For every $T\to\mathcal U$, the opens $T_i$ cover $T$ by [lem-sfb-open-substack-unions]. Each $W_i\times_{\mathcal U_i}T_i\to T_i$ is surjective by the chosen representable surjectivity of $a_i$. It is an open part of $W\times_{\mathcal U}T$, so every point of every $T_i$ lies in the image of $W\times_{\mathcal U}T\to T$. Since the $T_i$ cover $T$, this map is surjective. This uses precisely the scheme-test definition of surjectivity in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus), surjectivity of the union atlas; scheme-test convention of the cited definition.

proof.text: Now $\mathcal U$ is algebraic and has the representable surjective etale scheme atlas $a:W\to\mathcal U$. The reverse implication of [lem-sfb-unramified-diagonal-etale-atlas] proves that its relative diagonal over $S$ is unramified. This includes the case $I=\varnothing$: the union and $W$ are empty, and the scheme-chart and surjectivity checks above are vacuous on their empty tests.

If $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal X$ is an open substack with unramified relative diagonal, its representative occurs among the $\mathcal U_i$ by definition of $I$. The containment $\mathcal U_i\subseteq\mathcal U$ furnished by [lem-sfb-open-substack-unions] therefore gives $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal U$ (containment of full substacks is invariant under equivalence over $\mathcal X$). This is the required maximality.

source.place: Tag 0DSM (lemma-open-DM-locus), largest-open assertion, using the union property of Tag 05UQ (lemma-union-open-substacks).
